screens.why: Opening (sheet label 'opening'; clips-panel counts it in screen 1): about 9 s of Hogwarts castle and a broom flight before I learn whose site this is. Gorgeous, but I'd hit Skip intro.
The name lands big in blackletter over a glowing wave. The one-line pitch and 'self-taught high-school quant' tell me who this is in 3 s.
A porthole iris opens onto the Black Pearl, then the 'The Crossing' title card. About 6 s of picture with no information.
The 'A research journal in four acts' contents list orients me fast, although the film-coded act names don't say where the projects are.
'A builder of quantitative systems.' is the right headline. The sub-heads (Process over outcome, Intellectual honesty) are easy to skim.
The lower about columns are small grey text, but 'How the methodology was earned.' and the night-harbour plate pull me on.
The journey steps swap the plate (harbour to storm) and move a path diagram forward as I scroll. It feels alive.
'They failed out-of-sample' is a candid hook, and the teal wave lighting up in the plate is a nice beat.
After step 4 the screen drains to a dark band with a sliver of wave and a caption. Two seconds of nothing.
The second act card in 40 s. The torn-paper reveal of the lecture hall is pretty, but it's another picture before the work.
The 'The Workshop' title over the hall, then a near-black screen (clip 33, frames 2-3). I'd think the page had stalled.
At last the work: 'Led by what survived scrutiny.' over the astronaut-pen plate. Strong and direct.
The seven-part validation gauntlet list beside a chalkboard of hypothesis bars. Catnip for an engineer.
The flagship 'Quantitative Trading Research' card has a clear problem statement and a moody corridor plate.
A Rancho-style blueprint diagram and real numbers. Credible and fun.
Chalk notes on the stats and 'What is a machine?' written on the board. Witty, and it moves.
The second flagship (Automated Strategy Research Pipeline) reuses the first card's template, but the substance is new.
The Optuna blueprint plus 3,000+ resamples and a 25 % holdout. Dense, but it's the evidence I'd want.
The 'See the thesis, not just read it.' chart draws in and promises a backtest-vs-edge demo.
The chart finishes and the homemade-drone photo slides in, which is a nice surprise. The lower part of clip 54 is briefly empty.
The 'What I can actually do.' skills map is exactly what a recruiter scans for.
The tail of the skills grid: tiny three-column text beside a tall blueprint. I'd skim and leave.
'The kill-list': killed and never retuned. The best hook on the page for an engineer.
Killed strategies carry status tags, and a lens follows down the list. Honest and specific.
The 'Three films and a game' interlude is about 90 % empty dark screen with a small heading, and the egg-hunt invite is in fine print. This is where I'd close the tab.
The Black Pearl by moonlight is gorgeous. The first film plate is a treat.
A quote plus a paragraph of fan reflection. Filler for a recruiter.
The yellow scooter at Pangong Lake uses the same plate, quote and paragraph template. Seen it.
A red-tinted Dead Eye plate. The label hints at a game, but nothing on screen shows what to aim at.
The quill writing 'HARRY POTTER' is a nice touch, but this is the fourth plate in the same template.
Hogwarts Express plus a quote: pattern fatigue. A gold dot drifting across the dark is the only hook.
The third act card (RDR2 golden hour). I know this move by now.
The 'The Frontier' title card, then a near-black screen (clip 84, frames 2-3).
'Discipline, service, and a trained eye.' over a warm sunrise shows a new side of the person.
Concrete specifics (varsity cross country, wrestling weights) and a sketch map. Varied.
Small monospace lists next to a repeated horse silhouette. It's getting long.
The 'What's in the satchel' inventory icons look clickable, and a WANTED poster with his name drops in. Fun.
The parchment wipe is slick, but 'Thinking in public, soon.' tells me there's nothing to read yet.
Draft journal entries with faint sketches that draw themselves. Nice texture, but nothing to open.
More draft titles. I'm skimming past.
A forest-silhouette wipe into the gang's camp, then 'In their words.' Social proof is what I want.
Quotes from named teachers and an advisor. Credible and short.
The quotes fade over a dim camp, then the campfire burns a black hole into the photo. It reads as a glitch.
The fourth act card (Great Hall, 'The Light'), then a near-black screen with a tiny parchment at the bottom.

The last two principles give way to the contact pitch, so I can see the end.
Clear contact: one sentence, an email pill and GitHub. The floating-candle initials are a classy touch.
Film-style credits in tiny low-contrast text on black.

acts.feel: A long toll before the name: about 9 s at 1440 and 8 s at 1024. It's well shot, but a recruiter is reaching for Skip intro.
A big name, a clear pitch and a living wave. It reads fast, and nothing pushes me on until I scroll.

acts.feel: Varied textures (sunrise, sketch map, satchel, poster, parchment wipe, forest wipe, campfire), but it runs 12-13 screens, the journal is all drafts, and it ends in a glitchy burn.

findings.finding: The 'Three films and a game' interlude screen is about 90 % empty dark with a small heading. The page's only explicit invitation to play (12 easter eggs, the drone flies, Dead Eye) is fine print here, more than two minutes in. A skimmer leaves here without ever learning there's a game.

Four act title cards, each 6-8 s of full-bleed image plus a big title and no information. The first is cinematic. By the third (RDR2 'The Frontier') and fourth (Great Hall 'The Light') they feel seen-it, and they sit right where a busy visitor decides whether to stay.

Near-black or nearly empty frames at almost every act hand-off: just a sliver of wave, a strip of photo at the bottom edge, or a tiny parchment on black. At a glance they read as 'the page ended' or 'still loading'.
The four film plates use the identical template (plate, caption, quote, two-paragraph reflection). Only the first lands. The rest is fan content in the middle of a recruiting page.

The principles map scrolls at a low capture frame rate (clips-panel fps 4.1-5.6 at 1440 and 5.1-6.7 at 1024, against 10-20 elsewhere), so the parchment likely stutters. The map also holds still for about 6 s on arrival (1440 #112-#113, 1024 #105-#107).

In About at 1024 the three narrow serif columns turn into a wall, and the compass emblem drifts through the column gutter, crowding the 'Intellectual honesty' and 'A cross-cultural lens' text. At 1440 it sits in the gutter but is less cramped.
The Dead Eye plate shows no targets or X marks during the scroll at either width, so the game reads as just a red-tinted photo with a caption.

The opening runs about 8-9 s (play screen, castle, broom flight, sea) before the name appears. A Skip intro link exists, but this persona would rather have the name first. clips-panel shows a 383 ms frame gap at the 1440 name reveal (#5) and 483 ms on the 1024 play screen (#1).
In the campfire-to-Hogwarts burn, an irregular black hole opens in the photo while 'HARRY POTTER' already sits above the RDR2 caption. At first sight it reads as a render glitch, not a transition.
The 'A WANTED POSTER' caption is clipped under the nav band while the journal page holds for the 2 s heading stop.
The same astronaut-pen-on-the-desk photo heads both Work and the kill-list. Reuse is noticeable when only 50 seconds apart.
The tail of the skills grid is a wall of tiny three-column text beside a tall blueprint, with low contrast at a glance.
Writing ('Thinking in public, soon.') is all draft titles with nothing to open. Three screens of dead end for a reader.
The credits are tiny, low-contrast text on black and unreadable in a skim.
The interactive affordances (Egg hunt 0/12, 'Take off', the 'Dead Eye' pill, 'Lumos') are so small that they can't be read in the screencast frames. I could only read them in the static 1024 scenes.
Journey step 4 and the Kraken's-storm wave compete on one screen (clips-panel lists two scroll stars overlapping for 1.2 s). It reads as a busy hand-off rather than a clean beat.
